reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let d,q ∈ ℕ satisfy 2q + 1 < d. Put n = q + 1 and r = n, with r regarded as a real number. Let D = ℝ^d and E = ℝ^n with their Euclidean structures, let Ω = (Fin n → D), and let μ = ⨂_{b∈Fin n} γ_D, where γ_D is the centered standard Gaussian law on D. Let M be the real square-matrix algebra indexed, in each direction, by Fin n × Fin n; thus its matrices have size n² × n².

For i ∈ Fin d and k ∈ Fin n define
  L = 2r + 3 log(1000d),
  α_i = ((i + 1 - 1/2)π)/d,
  t_i(k) = 1 if k = 0, and t_i(k) = √2 cos(k α_i) otherwise.
All natural-number entries in these real formulas are cast to ℝ, and i and k denote the zero-based integer values of their Fin indices. For ω ∈ Ω let x_i(ω) ∈ E have coordinate x_i(ω)_b = ω(b)_i. Define
  Y_i(ω) = d⁻¹ [(x_i(ω)x_i(ω)ᵀ) ⊗ (t_i t_iᵀ)] if ‖x_i(ω)‖² ≤ L,
  Y_i(ω) = 0 otherwise,
  m_i = ∫_Ω Y_i(ω) dμ(ω),
  Z_i(ω) = Y_i(ω) - m_i.
Here ⊗ is the Kronecker product with the x-factor first and the t-factor second. The truncation includes equality at L, and the other branch is the zero matrix.

For Boolean values c,e define
  w_c(i) = cos((2q + 1)α_i) if c = true, and w_c(i) = 1 if c = false,
  σ_e = -1 if e = true, and σ_e = 1 if e = false,
  S_{c,e}(ω) = σ_e ∑_{i∈Fin d} w_c(i) Z_i(ω),
  R_* = 2r(L + 1)/d.
For every real s and every pair of Boolean values c,e, set
  G(ω) = exp_M(s S_{c,e}(ω)),
  MX = ∫_Ω G(ω) dμ(ω),
  B = r² exp_ℝ(|s| d R_*).
Then G is Bochner integrable with respect to μ; MX is positive definite; tr(MX) = ∫_Ω tr(G(ω)) dμ(ω); and 0 < tr(MX) ≤ B. The exponential exp_M is the power-series exponential of the matrix algebra, exp_ℝ is the scalar exponential, and tr is the ordinary unnormalized trace. Positive definite means symmetric with a strictly positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector.
record_scope: Reconstruction only; no proof or source-equivalence verdict.
scopes: All displayed integrals use precisely the finite product Gaussian measure μ. x_i(ω) has coordinates ω(b)_i; converting to or from WithLp preserves these coordinates. Truncation is by the Euclidean vector norm squared, with the inclusive condition ‖x_i(ω)‖²≤L and zero outside. In the Kronecker product, x_ix_iᵀ is the first factor and t_it_iᵀ the second, so entry ((b,k),(b′,k′)) is d⁻¹x_i(b)x_i(b′)t_i(k)t_i(k′) inside the truncation. The first cosine coordinate is t_i(0)=1; later coordinates use √2cos(kα_i). The angle uses the explicitly added one: α_i=(i+1−1/2)π/d for zero-based i. c selects either the cosine weight at frequency 2q+1 or constant weight one. e selects one global scalar sign outside the entire sum. exp_M is the matrix-algebra power-series exponential, whereas exp_ℝ is scalar. Trace is the ordinary diagonal sum without division by dimension. MX.PosDef means symmetry and strict positivity on nonzero vectors. Any scoped matrix norm is the Euclidean/L2 operator norm. The parameter s includes zero and negative values; |s| occurs in B.
